tasks.task: Measure the space and write the brief

items.when: At the very start, when the owner has photos and a vague goal but no measured plan
When the owner cannot describe the look, to pin down tone and feel in four answers
When the owner sets no limits, to fix firm rules for budget, keep-list and style before any plan
When the job has several people involved, to get a one-page brief and who decides what
Before you move anything, to watch where people really sit, queue and enter

tasks.task: Plan the layout of a cafe, salon, studio or shop floor

items.when: When you have measurements and need zones, furniture sizes, walkways, turning space and exits
Before the layout, to map a visit from the door to the till with the snags at each stage
When people queue in the wrong place or miss the counter, to find what in the layout misleads them
When the plan fits the furniture but not how people meet, wait and move

tasks.task: Lay out a small office or workroom

items.when: When desks, storage and walkways must fit a measured room with clear exits
When the desks need task light at the right level and glare kept off screens
When staff keep working around the room, to name what gets in their way

tasks.task: Write a lighting plan for a room

items.when: When the room needs general, task and accent light with positions, warmth and dimming
When the owner names a feeling, to set what the light and colour must do to support it
When the room looks flat, to study where the light falls and what should stand out

tasks.task: Choose a colour scheme for a room

items.when: When wall, trim and accent colours must be set with the light they will be seen in
When you know the feeling wanted, to get a small palette with one job per colour
When two moods are in play, to see the colour and image choices each would bring

tasks.task: Show the owner the planned look before they spend

items.when: When the owner wants to see the look before spending and you need prompts for an image tool
When the look is undecided, to compare three mood board directions and merge a pick
When one room idea should be tried as four different treatments
When you have a photo of the real room and want the changes drawn onto it
When the images show things the room cannot have, to turn each fault into a prompt line
When the concept should start from the owner's own photo of the room
When you want to explore moods quickly before fixing one
When you have the window size, products, goal and dates and need one idea, a focal point and a prop list
Before the plan, to cut the window to one idea, one feeling and one thing to look at
When the window needs one sign that reads from across the street
When the window sells a product and says nothing of how the shop feels inside

tasks.task: Plan an in-store table, shelf or wall display

items.when: When a table, shelf or wall needs a focal point, grouping and heights planned from measurements
When you have sales and margins, to give best sellers the best space shelf by shelf
When the shop is a charity or resale store and needs display zones tied to price bands

tasks.task: Plan a year of window themes

items.when: When a shop wants twelve months of themes tied to its sales dates, with props it can reuse
When the windows must line up with the shop's promotions, to set the push for each period first
Once a month, starting two weeks before the change date in the window calendar
When this month's theme needs its own plan, prop list and set-up order
When staff will change the window themselves and need exact steps and what to do if it goes wrong

tasks.task: Plan a market stall or pop-up display

items.when: When a table or stall needs height, a focal point and a set-up order that fits in a car
When the stall needs a banner or sign that reads from the end of the aisle
When the owner asks how much stock to bring to a one-off event

tasks.task: Lay out window and in-store signs

items.when: Before any sign, to map each point where a first-time visitor must choose a way
When signs are part of a display and need sizes, heights and positions
When a sign or price list carries a lot of text and needs a grid and a short type list
When the sign has no picture, to try a type-only version that reads from far away
When the sign is for an event and you want a guided run to a layout and export checklist
Before the signs are printed, to build three real-size layouts with the real words and compare them
When a sign is drafted, to check type size, spacing and line length where it is read

tasks.task: Style a holiday let room for photos and guests

items.when: When a host wants rooms that photograph well and are comfortable and safe on a small budget
When the rooms look dull in photos and need warmer, layered light
When a photographer will shoot the rooms and needs one clear brief
When the room is tidy but does not feel welcoming to someone arriving tired

tasks.task: Set up a photo or content corner

items.when: When a corner must fit a backdrop, a stool and room to stand back with a phone
When the corner needs even, flattering light at the times the owner films
When the corner is for product shots, to set a style sheet the backdrop and props must match

tasks.task: Cost the refresh and set the order of work

items.when: When the plans are approved and you need a costed list that reuses owned items first
When the wish list is over budget, to pick the set of items worth most within the limit
Before the owner commits, to show two ways to split the budget and order the work, with totals that add up
When you have two or more quotes for the same items, to compare price, lead time and risk
Before one large buy such as a counter or sofa, to see the real cost and a small test first
When the owner has a reopening date, to correct the estimate by how such jobs really go

tasks.task: Sort which changes need a trade or building control

items.when: Before costing or starting, to sort each change into owner can do it, needs a trade or must ask
When trades have quoted, to compare their proposals and terms side by side
When you have two or more quotes pasted, to get one table and what each needs up front

tasks.task: Run a room refresh from brief to reopening

items.when: When an owner wants a refresh with a budget and a date and needs the steps in order
When the order of work must keep the business open as long as possible
Once work has started, to track spend and dates against the plan and the likely final cost
When the plan has no slack, to test the dates against jobs like it

tasks.task: Check the space works for every visitor

items.when: When you need walkway widths, turning space and counter heights checked on the plan
When the space hosts events, to plan step-free routes and what the venue must confirm
When visitors cannot find the toilet, till or exit without asking

tasks.task: Review an existing space and list the fixes

items.when: When you have photos and measurements and must find pinch points and wasted areas
When reviews mention noise, seating or queues, to count the themes before you plan
When complaints are piling up, to turn them into ranked questions the redesign must answer
When you walk the space as a customer, to log each stage and where it snags
When the owner blames the decor and the real fault is where people are made to stand

always.when: Before any plan for a business with a live site, so the room matches its colours and voice
Before any sign or price list is printed, to catch typos and names spelt two ways

helpers.when: When signs, menus or window graphics need finished print-ready artwork
When the display depends on stock levels, margins and what the shop needs to sell
When the holiday let also needs its listing, pricing and guest messages sorted
When the finished space or its products need a planned photo set
When the refresh grows into building work with several trades and inspections
When the reopening needs local promotion and a launch plan

gaps: The library is thin for this role: about 40 items fit, most of them adjacent, and the four kit skills carry the core work
No library item plans a room layout from measurements: zones, walkways, clearances and exits
No library item writes a lighting plan or picks lamps, colour temperature and dimming
No library item chooses paint, flooring or finishes for a real room; the palette items set a feeling only
No library item plans a shop window or does visual merchandising beyond shelf facings
No library item plans a market stall, pop-up or exhibition stand
No library item styles a holiday let or writes a room-by-room photo shot list
No library item draws a scaled floor plan or elevation, or offers two or three layouts to compare
No library item checks a plan for fire exits, access widths or furniture fire labels
No library item builds a reuse-first shopping list or sources furniture and fittings
No library item briefs a trade with a scope of work or keeps a snagging list
No mind covers interior or retail display design, and no tool guide covers room planning or 3D room tools
